function: Near-field mmWave beam training: selects the analog precoder codeword (angle and distance) directly from sub-6 GHz uplink pilots, bypassing channel estimation (pp. 1, 5-6)
system: Multiuser OFDM; mmWave BS with 256-antenna ULA (ELAA), hybrid precoding, 30 GHz; sub-6 GHz BS with 32 antennas, 5.5 GHz; single-antenna users; no RIS (pp. 3, 9)
method: Supervised classification: CNN plus GNN network NMBEnet (angle and distance branches), cross-entropy loss, Adam, labels from exhaustive search, trained offline (pp. 7-9)
data_channel: Remcom Wireless InSite ray tracing in its bundled 'MIMO Example' scenario; 20,000 samples, 95% training and 5% validation; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data (p. 9)
test_conditions: Single WI scene; 20,000 samples split 95/5 train/validation; no separate test set stated; evaluation sweeps uplink power, sub-6 GHz antenna count and BS location (pp. 9-12)
baselines: Classical: exhaustive near-field codebook search (upper bound). Learned: FCNN and CNN beam predictors of Alrabeiah and Alkhateeb [20] using sub-6 GHz channels (p. 10)
metrics: Average downlink sum rate per subcarrier, effective sum rate (net of pilot overhead), and beam estimation accuracy (angle, distance, overall) (pp. 9-10)
complexity: Table II gives parameters per layer, from 6.14x10^3 (first convolution) to 1.17x10^6 (first FC layer); no FLOPs or runtime (p. 10)
openness: none; no link to code or data, only the commercial Wireless InSite website is cited (p. 13)
q1_support: p. 9: "The WI software employs ray tracing". Channels come from Remcom Wireless InSite on its bundled MIMO Example scene; the paper uses no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100 or DeepMIMO model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "training, with 95% used for training and 5% for validation." One WI scene; Figs. 12, 13 and 17 (pp. 10-12) sweep uplink power, sub-6 GHz antenna number and BS location, and the paper never states that a trained network is tested on a scenario, band or configuration unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 10: "the FCNN structure proposed in [20], which utilizes sub-6". Baseline 1 is exhaustive search, Baselines 2 and 3 are the FCNN and CNN of [20]; all compared on accuracy and sum rate in Figs. 12-16 (pp. 10-12).
q4_support: p. 10: "Nimbers of parameters". Table II lists parameters per layer, from 6.14x10^3 (first convolution) to 1.17x10^6 (first FC layer); no FLOPs or runtime are given.
q5_support: p. 13: "Remcom, Wireless InSite. [Online]." The paper cites only the commercial ray-tracing tool and gives no link to code or data; its channels are generated by the authors, not taken from a public dataset.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv v1 (23 Apr 2024) of the NMBEnet paper; the text does not print the DOI, so the match rests on the title and topic. Area 3: the network picks the BS analog precoder beam. q1 is borderline: Wireless InSite is a commercial ray tracer on a scene bundled with the software, not on the list, so the reviewer may confirm. q2: no separate test set is described, and the paper does not say whether the network was retrained for each antenna count or BS location. The Table II header is misspelled Nimbers in the paper.
